It’s hard to find a place these days without any form of technology. Not only has it changed the way people live, but it’s also made an impact on different aspects of society. Business, for example, have benefited the most out of the rapid advancements in technology. Even small business nowadays tend to conduct their operations via some form of program or machine.
As businesses continue to prosper, the technological changes become increasingly essential to their daily operations. But how exactly do these changes in technology affect businesses?
Reduction in Operating Costs
Advancements in technology have made it possible for businesses to automate even just back-office functions. This allows for faster and more accurate results at a fraction of the time and price it would have cost without such automation. With regular updates and developments, cost optimization is within reach for even small businesses.
Improved Employee Productivity
Businesses rely on computer programs and software in order to process more data at a quicker pace. When utilized with hardware that’s intended to enhance connectivity, such as high-speed cables and high-capacity docking stations, employees are able to increase their performance and daily output. Aside from causing an increase in employee productivity, developments in technology also lower labor costs and improve the company’s overall performance.
Better Security on Sensitive Information
Technology creates environments that provide utmost security for sensitive information involving both the business and its consumers. Nowadays, many kinds of business software come equipped with their own tools and features. Aside from being secure, these tools are also user-friendly.
Expansion of Customer Base
Even small businesses are now able to reach national or even international markets. Online shops are abundant on the internet, and consumers are now able to purchase products and services worldwide with just a few quick clicks of the mouse. Technological developments have paved the way for customer bases to be expanded on a global scale and have certainly changed the way consumers shop.
Easier Adaptability
Markets share the commonality of being prone to change, and those that make heavy use of technology tend to undergo the most change over time. Hence, it has become important for technology-dependent businesses to know how to adapt to quick shifts in the market at any given moment.
Modern advancements have certainly made adapting to market changes a lot easier, with solutions that are straightforward and designed to aid in the ability of a business to adapt. Now, when the market you’re in shows any signs of change, all you need to do is to implement these ready technological solutions into your workflow. Operations will adapt to this new workflow as necessary.
Communication-Process Improvement
Nowadays, customers are able to utilize texts, calls, emails, and even instant messaging to communicate with companies. This simplified communication process between a business and its consumers allows a faster flow of goods and services, facilitating improvements and addressing urgent concerns.
But this communication-process improvement brought about by technology does not only positively impact the relationship between the business and its consumers. It also keeps employees within the company connected and up-to-date on the goings on within their own departments and the company.
Increased Possibility of Outsourcing
Outsourcing is what businesses turn to when there isn’t ample space, facilities, or manpower for day-to-day operations to be run successfully. The most common functions that companies outsource are customer service and technical support. In outsourcing these functions, businesses can focus on performing those that they do best while also lowering operational costs.
Technology has simplified and improved business operations for decades. Even though it continues to evolve, it isn’t always a straightforward development, so it’s important for companies to stay on top of technological changes that may affect everyday processes. Regardless, new solutions are often welcomed as the benefits they give to any small or large business in the long run are often huge.

The Impact of Technology on a Business Environment
Just a few decades ago, if you walked into an office, you’d see employees tapping away on typewriters and chatting away on landline phones. If one worker wanted to communicate with another, it meant getting up and walking to that person’s desk, rather than sending a HipChat or an email. But technology continues to evolve, always impacting the way business leaders hire, market, budget and protect their investments.
Impact on Human Resources
Experts have long predicted technology will someday replace many of the jobs done by humans. However, history has shown that as jobs become obsolete, new opportunities open up. Today’s students are encouraged to prepare for technology-based jobs like data analysis and computer programming, whereas four decades ago they would have been steered toward an education for an administrative or a sales position. Technology has also transformed hiring, with the internet allowing workers to complete their duties from home or another remote location. This has the added benefit of giving businesses access to a global talent pool that allows them to hire specialized, experienced workers at affordable rates.
Impact on Customer Outreach
Thanks to social media and the internet, reaching consumers is easier than ever. Using a do-it-yourself website tool and various social platforms, even the newest small business can post content that helps interested customers find them. Instead of paying third parties for advertising in print or electronic media, today’s businesses are in charge of their own customer outreach. The result is a reduced cost that levels the playing field between large corporations and startups.

Impact on Operating Costs
Another area where the technological environment has evened things out is the overhead associated with running a business. Companies sell their items online, which means they don’t need a brick-and-mortar storefront. The cost of starting a new business has dropped dramatically in recent years, since founders can now launch a venture from home as a side gig. There’s no need to travel to land new clients, because researching and reaching out to potential customers can all be done online. And, instead of hiring a bookkeeper or an assistant, entrepreneurs find that software handles all of the early-stage functions they need.
Impact on Security
One area where the impact of technology on business has brought both positives and negatives is security. Having so much information on internet-connected servers means it’s susceptible to theft. Data breaches can be devastating to a new business without the resources to handle it, with the average incident costing small businesses about $36,000. Businesses now need to put significant effort into securing their networks and all connected devices, which often means paying a monthly fee for top-tier cloud hosting and software to keep equipment safe. This has also opened up opportunities for tech specialists in the cybersecurity arena, where experts are in high demand.
The Day to Day Impact on Business
Today's technology has completely changed some businesses as well as creating entire business niches that never even existed before. Business owners run their companies from laptops, tablets and smartphones, never even considering opening a brick-and-mortar presence.
The daily environment in existing businesses has changed immensely, too. Office workers often spend part of their week working remotely from home or on the road. Business meetings no longer mean driving long distances as teleconferencing means getting everyone together online. Many offices are now paperless, keeping all their documents in the cloud, while others use online chat technology to keep teams in constant communication.
